title: 2D Pattern (DXF) Import/Export
content: Import (Add) Export **** DXF is a standard file format of industrial CAD patterns and stores 2D pattern information. DXF is currently available in Yuka, Gerber, Lectra, StyleCAD, Optitex, PAD System, etc. **DXF-AAMA, DXF-ASTM, Standard DXF files of AutoCAD and Adobe Illustrator** files are compatible with most 2D CAD softwares. **** #### **Import (Add)** 1. Click the File ▶ Import / Import (Add) / Export ▶ **DXF** in the top menu. 2. Select the DXF file and click **Open**. 3. Set the details and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **File Format** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569253105689) Select the format of the DXF file being imported: Standard DXF / AAMA / ASTM. _(Previously auto-detected by CLO)_ **Scale** | Select the unit used in the pattern CAD. **Rotation** | Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. **Option** **** **** | **Import Pattern Annotation** | Import Pattern Annotation information together. **Auto-Trace as Internal Line** | The entire baseline is traced as an Internal Line. **Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line** | Check this option when the pattern's Cutting lines and Sewing lines are changed. * The Cutting line and Sewing line may change depending on the export option setting of the pattern CAD. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001304047/03_____________.png) **Include Notches** | When changing the Sewing line and Cutting Line, the notch is moved together. **Import Notch to** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569253105689) Decide the imported notch placement on Seam Allowance, Pattern Outline, or Both. **Notch Position** | Fixed notch at a specific position, or place a notch at a position by ratio. **Auto Distribute** | Closely rearrange the patterns in the DXF file. **Optimize All Curve Points** | Optimizes the number of curve points in the DXF file. **Convert to Seam Allowance** | Import CAD seam allowance to CLO seam allowance. The default setting is applied to the type of start, end or edge seam allowance that is not supported by CLO. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643520144921)**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569253105689) This option has been removed from the menu starting from version **2026.1**. DXF Seam Allowance is now automatically read and converted into [**Custom Seam Allowance**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013370408-Edit-Seam-Allowance-Properties) (Locked status). Unlock it for further editing. **Remove Non-Grading Points** | Optimize the number of points by deleting Straight/Curve Points that have no grading information. This option is only required for AAMA-format DXF files which is different from CLO's default curve points. **** #### **Export** 1. Click the File ▶ Export ▶ **DXF** in the top menu. 2. Set the file name, save the path, and click OK. 3. Set the details and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Select Pattern** | Select the size group you want to export from among the grading size groups applied to the file. Only one Size Group can be selected and exported per file. **DXF Format** | Set the export format: DXF-AAMA, DXF-ASTM, Standard DXF. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569253105689) _(If you previously used "Gerber (DXF-AAMA)", select DXF-AAMA — it produces the same output)_ **Size format** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59569253105689) Export grading information included in the DXF file, or separately as a Rule File. (If you previously used "Rule File (Lectra)", select Rule File — it is the same option) **Scale** | Set the unit of the pattern. **Rotation** | Rotate the entire pattern clockwise/counterclockwise. **Option** | **Export without Grading** | Export the current size only, excluding grading information. **Export without Baselines** | Export patterns except for baselines. **Duplicate Notch on Seam Allowance** | Duplicate the notch on the outline of the pattern to the seam allowance. **Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line** | The type of sewing line and the cutting line defined in CLO and Pattern CAD may be different. In this case, when exporting to DXF, the cutting line and the sewing line are replaced and exported. **Convert Curve Point to Straight Point (AI Only)** | When DXF is imported from AI (Adobe Illustrator), the curve information does not come in properly, which may distort part of the pattern. In this case, it can be solved by converting all the curved points of the pattern to straight points. **Optimize All Curve Points** | Easily modify the curve by optimizing the number of curve points added on the line segment. **Export Pattern Bounding Box** **(Single Bounding Box/** **Separate Pattern Bounding Box)** | By exporting the pattern with the bounding box, conveniently edit the image when working in Photoshop, Illustrator, etc. **Export Selected Patterns** | Only the selected pattern is exported not the entire pattern.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting DXF files, a standard format for industrial CAD patterns, ensuring compatibility across various 2D CAD software.

title: Nest Patterns
content: ### **List of Contents** Switch Mode Nest Pattern Nest Option Nest Settings Auto-Arrange Labels Manual Nesting Reset Default Arrangement Snapshot #### Efficiently layout patterns and check fabric consumption to use the least amount of fabric. **** #### **Switch Mode** 1. Switch to Print Layout mode on the top-right corner of CLO. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59644578529561) **Rotate** button at the bottom-right corner to switch the marker orientation between **Vertical** and **Horizontal**. → In **Vertical** mode, Width runs along the X-axis and Length along the Y-axis, while in **Horizontal** mode, the axes are swapped. → Pattern placement and grainline alignment are preserved during the switch. #### #### **Nest Patterns** **All Fabrics** 1. Click the ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest Pattern** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are efficiently placed on the fabric and the calculated value is displayed. 2. Click the **Stop Nesting** tool in the toolbar. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **Current Fabric** Selectively re-nest a specific fabric while preserving the results of other fabrics. 1. Click and hold ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest All Fabrics** tool to switch to ![Nest Patterns On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429419417) **Nest Current Fabric** tool. → Only the selected fabric in Print Layout Editor will be nested. All other fabrics will remain unchanged. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **📝****Note:** * Directly click the pattern ▶ Drag it within the set fabric width to place it or place the pattern using [Align](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000306628-Align) and [Distribute](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000295167-Distribute). * Instead of waiting for nesting to complete, stop directly at any point in time to place patterns to save nesting time. * The number of calculations varies depending on the number of patterns. Higher counts give optimal arrangement results, but larger numbers of patterns require more calculations and take more time. Moving one space of the progress bar means that once the calculation has been completed. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** #### **Nest Option** CLO automatically identifies the visual characteristics of textures and prints, and optimizes Nesting to ensure continuity with maximum efficiency. 1. Set how the pattern is matched by right-clicking on it in Print Layout mode or under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Texture Based** | CLO automatically detects the texture placement on each pattern and nests them with optimal efficiency by ensuring texture alignment. The same arrangement is consistently applied across all sizes based on how the patterns are stacked. **Print Based** | Similar to the above Texture-Based Matching, but with the added Print. **Lock in Place** | Locks the Base Size placement in Print Layout as is, while the remaining patterns follow the Texture-Based concept. **📝****Note:** When Pattern Matching is set, the texture movement is restricted when using Edit Texture tool to prevent misalignment. However, the restriction on texture movement can be unlocked using the Pattern Matching Lock option under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode if needed. #### #### **Nest Settings** 1. Click the **Nest Setting** tool in the toolbar. → Nesting Options appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set each property. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Nesting** | **Number of Garment** | Nest grading patterns on the fabric for mass production. By clicking the Select Grading button, manually set the size and quantity(amount) of the grading patterns to be nested. **📝****Note:****** Different colors can be displayed for each grading size on the fabric and you can check the size names. ([**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) • Display grading colors: 2D Pattern Display » Show Grading Random Color icon • Display grading names: 2D Information Display » Show Grading Size icon **Group Each Sizes** | Click the **Group Each Sizes** option to nest patterns by grouping the graded sizes separately. (**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/JcJVKJlNuNw)) **Colorway** | Nest patterns of all colorways on the fabric or click Select Colorway on the right to place only the selected colorway on the fabric. **Grain Direction** | **1-way** | Place the pattern in one orientation along the original grain direction **2-way** | Place the pattern in the opposite orientation that is 180 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **4-way** | Place the pattern in four different orientations that are each 90 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **One Bundle One Direction** | **OFF**(Default) | Patterns within the same size/bundle can be placed in different orientations (randomly) to achieve maximum fabric efficiency. **ON** | All pattern pieces belonging to a single size (one bundle) will be restricted to the same orientation. While the nest as a whole uses 2-way or 4-way logic, each individual garment bundle maintains a consistent direction. **Buffer Spacing** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) Set non-uniform spacing on each side of the pattern**.** • Left / Right — Set the buffer value along the width axis. • Top / Bottom — Set the buffer value along the length axis. Click the Link icon to apply a uniform value to all four sides at once. Use the color chip or hex input to set the outline color. ※ Note: The buffer remains anchored to the pattern when rotated. **Pattern Dimension** | **Actual** | Place the pattern in its actual size. **Shrinkage** **/Growth** | Place the pattern with the shrinkage rate applied. **Preferred Outline** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) Set the boundary line for nesting. **📝****Note:** Add shrinkage line and delete baseline from ver 2026.1. **Seam Allowance Position** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) Set the seam allowance position on the original pattern or shrinkage pattern. **📝****Note:** This feature is disabled if fabric shrinkage is not applied. **Information** | **Unit** | Set the units. **Fabric** | **Width** | Adjust the width of the fabric. **Length** | Check the total length of the fabric on which the pattern is placed. **Marker Length** | Set the length of the fabric manually to nest the pattern only up to the length of the set fabric. ([![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777) ](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) **Efficiency** | **Consumption** | Based on 100% of the total fabric, the fabric area consumed for the pattern is calculated as % **Remnant** | The remainder after subtracting the area consumed by the pattern is calculated as a %. **Area** | **Pattern Placed** | Check the pattern area placed on the fabric. **Remnant** | Check the remaining area where no pattern is placed. #### **📝****Note:** Removed **Pattern Dimension** feature**** from **CLO 2026.1.** #### ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) #### **Auto-Arrange Labels** 1. Click the**Auto-Arrange Labels** tool in the toolbar. → Annotations and information labels dynamically shift and rearrange themselves inside their respective pattern outlines. _**✨Tip:** Use the _[_**Edit Annotation tool**_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004324627-Pattern-Annotation) _to customize text or formatting in advance before auto-arranging._ #### ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568414128665) #### **Manual Nesting** 1. Click the **Manual Nesting** tool in the toolbar. → Activate the mode in which patterns can be arranged and packed together without overlapping. All patterns stay inside the fabric roll boundary. 2. Arrange patterns using any of the following interactive controls. * **Free Move:** Press and drag patterns directly with the mouse cursor. * **Nudge Move:** Select the desired patterns and press the **Arrow keys** on your keyboard to shift them incrementally. * **Switch Selection:** While a pattern is selected, press **Shift + Arrow key** to instantly cycle through and select neighboring patterns for rapid editing. #### **Reset Default Arrangement** 1. Click the**Reset Default Arrangement** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are reset to the initial arrangement state. #### #### **Snapshot** 1. Click the**Snapshot** tool in the toolbar. → 2D Snapshot pop-up window appears. 2. Set the size along with other options for the snapshot. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Size** | **Preset** | Select from a variety of presets. **Orientation** | Select the paper orientation. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Set the unit of the print paper. **Resolution** | Set the resolution of the snapshot image. **Add'l Information** | Select the information that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Options** | Select the line that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Style** | Adjust the style of line to default Solid Line, Dotted Line, or Dashed Line. **Line Color** | Adjust the color of line. **Show Images** | Select the image that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Fabric Texture Opacity** | Adjust the opacity of the fabric and texture. **📝 Note:** Patterns and Internal Shapes with adhesion/bonding are classified separately in the **Bond** tab. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions on efficiently laying out patterns and optimizing fabric consumption in CLO, ensuring maximum material usage and minimal waste.

title: Trace
content: Trace (Line Mode) Trace as Pattern Trace as Internal Shape Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes Trace as Point of Measure (POM) Trace (Shape Mode) Trace Fill & Trace Trim Slice **** Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area/[guidelines ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360010960074)to Patterns. #### Trace (Line Mode) #### **Trace as Pattern** 1. Select the ![Trace On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642868738073) **Trace** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Select the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines to be traced. 3. Select the lines on both sides of a half-symmetry pattern to create a traced pattern that preserves the half-symmetry relationship and includes any Baselines and Internal Lines within the selected area. 4. Right-click on the selected Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines to access the pop-up menu. 5. Select **Trace as a Pattern**. →The selected Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines are traced as a Pattern. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Trace as Internal Shape** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as an Internal Shape**. →When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. **📝****Note:** To easily select a closed shape, double-click on the Internal Line. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes**. →The selected lines are traced as they are. **📝****Note:** Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Trace as**[**POM**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025716774-2D-%EC%A4%84%EC%9E%90-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines, Internal Lines or Outlines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected lines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as Point of Measure** → The selected line is traced as POM. → When more than two segments of different patterns are clicked, they are traced as a group POM. At this time, the connected points are randomly designated. #### Trace (Shape Mode) Use Shape Tracing to combine, cut, or split overlapping Patterns directly in the 2D Pattern Window. 1. Select the ![Trace On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642868738073) **Trace** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. In the **Trace** dialog, click **Shape** to switch to Shape mode. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Trace** Use ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642834579865) **Trace** to merge two or more overlapping Patterns into one new Pattern that follows the combined outline of all selected pieces. 1. Select two or more overlapping Patterns. 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642834579865) **Trace** buttonin the Trace dialog. → A preview of the merged Pattern outline follows the cursor. 3. Click to place the resulting Pattern in the 2D Pattern Window. → A new Pattern is created that covers the full area of all selected Patterns combined. → Any internal lines or shapes — such as holes, notches, or internal markings — that exist within the selected Patterns are carried over into the new Pattern. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Fill & Trace** Use ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642868740377) **Fill & Trace** to merge overlapping Patterns into one new solid Pattern. Any gaps or openings between the selected Patterns are automatically closed. Unlike **Trace** , internal lines or shapes within the original Patterns are not carried over to the result. 1. Select two or more overlapping Patterns. 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59642868740377) **Fill & Trace** button in the Trace dialog. → A preview of the filled, merged Pattern follows the cursor. 3. Click to place the resulting Pattern in the 2D Pattern Window. → A new solid Pattern is created from the combined area of all selected Patterns. → Gaps and openings between the selected pieces are closed. → Internal lines or shapes from the original Patterns are not included in the result. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Trim** Use ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643003512473) **Trim** to cut the shape of one Pattern out of another. The last Pattern you select acts as the cutting shape, and the result keeps only the parts of the other Patterns that were not covered by it. 1. Select two or more overlapping Patterns. Select the Pattern you want to use as the **cutting shape last**. → When you hover over the **Trim** icon, the cutting Pattern turns red so you can confirm the right one before clicking. 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643003512473) **Trim** button in the Trace dialog. → A preview of the trimmed Pattern(s) follows the cursor. 3. Click to place the resulting Patterns in the 2D Pattern Window. → The area covered by the cutting Pattern is removed from the other Patterns. → The remaining pieces are placed as a new Pattern. **📝****Note:** If the cutting Pattern sits entirely within another Pattern, a hole in the shape of the cutting Pattern is punched into the result instead. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** #### **Slice** Use ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643003516313) **Slice** to cut all selected Patterns apart wherever they overlap, turning each region into a separate piece. This is useful when you need each overlapping area as its own independent Pattern. 1. Select two or more overlapping Patterns. 2. Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59643003516313) **Slice** button in the Trace dialog. → A preview of the separated pieces follows the cursor. 3. Click to place the resulting Patterns in the 2D Pattern Window. → Every overlapping region is separated into its own individual Pattern piece. **** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to effectively use the Trace function to convert lines, shapes, and areas into patterns in various modes, including Line Mode and Shape Mode, for seamless design integration in your projects.

title: Fold 3D Garment
content: Auto Manual **** Fold your 3D garment easily. **** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59709639556633) #### **Auto** For best results, drape your garment on a T-pose avatar with the arms extended before folding. 1. Click the ![Fold 3D Garment On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59709679937177) **Fold 3D Garment** in the 3D toolbar. 2. If the garment is simulated on an avatar, click the **Lay Flat** button. → The garment is laid flat for simulation. * If the garment is already laid flat, click**Skip to Fold** to skip this step. 3. Select a garment type. → Default fold lines for the selected garment type are shown. **📝****Note:** Currently, only Shirts is available. More garment types will be added in future releases. 4. Enter the fold line dimensions, then click the **Fold Garment** button. → The garment is automatically folded along the specified fold lines. 5. To adjust the folded shape, click the **Unfold Garment** button to return the garment to its unfolded state, then update the fold line dimensions and apply them again. **** #### **Manual** 1. Switch to the Manual mode in the Fold 3D Garment window. 2. When a 3D garment is draped over an avatar, click the avatar with the Select/Move tool to [Delete](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000434168-Delete-Avatar) it. 3. To fold a 3D garment efficiently, arrange and set it by clicking each button below. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410129673369) | **Rotate X-Axis** | The tool rotates the 3D garment 90 degrees along the X-axis. When the 3D garment is in the air, it is moved to the center of the ground. **![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410135395481)**| **Flip Horizontally** | Flip the 3D garment horizontally to fold part of the garment above or below the guideline. If a garment is folded in the upward state, it may be unstable due to collision with the ground. It is recommended to fold it in the downward state and then turn it over again. **![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410124135065)**| **Optimize-Res Garment** | In order to efficiently fold the 3D garment, the Particle Distance and the Add'l Thickness - Collision are applied in batches with optimized values. Optimized values ​​are applied by default, and change as needed. **![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410129686297)**| **Set Physical Property for Spreading** | Set the proper physical property for spreading the 3D garment flat on the ground. **![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410135405593)**| **Set Physical Property for Folding** | Set the proper physical property for folding the 3D garment easily. 4. Click the ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59709760492569) **Fold** tool. 5. Click the start point of the line to be folded on the ground or the 3D garment, double click to end it. → The line is created, and the gizmo for rotation appears. 6. Click the gizmo axis (red or yellow-green) in the direction you want to fold to rotate it along the blue circle gizmo. → It rotates in that direction. 7. Simulate the garment. → The garment is simulated in a rotated state. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59709639559193)** **📝****Note:** * Click the ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4410144979481)**Fold (Selected)** tool to select and fold only a specific pattern piece. It is helpful when you want to fold a long sleeve one more time. * You can create the horizontal, vertical, and 45-degree guidelines by pressing the Shift on the keyboard while drawing the lines. * To delete the line while drawing, press the ESC on the keyboard. * Click the Fold (Selected) tool to select and fold only a specific pattern piece.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to easily fold 3D garments using both automatic and manual methods in your design software.

title: Check Sewing Length
content: **List of Contents** Check Sewing Length Result of Check Sewing Length Check Sewing Length Options **Check Sewing Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9f4cbaieuc \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021909768/mceclip0.png) **Check Sewing Length** tool to identify significant sewing length difference made during the Garment making process. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021909768/mceclip0.png) Check Sewing Length tool from the 2D Toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Check Sewing Length** ** Result of Check Sewing Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-c2bKFicduI \- Click to activate the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021909768/mceclip0.png) **Check Sewing Length** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021909768/mceclip0.png) **Check Sewing Length** tool is activated, the Sewing Lines with the sewing length difference larger than 3mm will be highlighted in red. **Check Sewing Length Options** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g9AIO9CfQNw** * **Length Difference ** \- Toggle on and assign value to the Length Difference to highlight and bold Sewing Lines when their sewing length difference is larger than the assigned value. * **Ratio Difference** \- Toggle on and assign value to the Ratio Difference to highlight and bold Sewing Lines when their sewing length difference is larger than the assigned ratio. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide on using the "Check Sewing Length" tool, including instructions, options, and instructional videos to enhance garment making accuracy.

title: Select/Move (3D)
content: ### **Objective** Select and move Patterns in the 3D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Select/Move** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000020407) **Select/Move** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ **Select/Move** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Select.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000020407) **Select/Move** 2. **** Click and drag a part of the 3D Garment while the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52765631211801) **Simulate** tool is activated. → The 3D Garment moves naturally and you may fine-tune your 3D Garment. 3. Or, click and drag a part of the 3D Garment while the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52765631211801) **Simulate** tool is deactivated. → The 3D window is converted to pattern arrangement mode and you may move the Garment as Patterns.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for selecting and moving patterns in the 3D window of the software, enabling users to fine-tune their garments effectively.

title: AI Image Generator

title: Is training available?
content: **Question** Is training available? Where can I learn CLO? **Answer** **CLO for Individual users** provides various online training resources on the CLO web as well as social media. **1.[CLO Academy Online](https://clo3d.geniussis.com/Registration.aspx):** Designed & created by the CLO 3D Design Team. _**Intro to CLO- Basic Apparel Design**_ and _**Intro to CLO- Basic Handbag Design**_ are currently available, with more offerings coming soon. These 2 paid courses go over all the techniques and concepts for creating garments and handbags in CLO. Throughout these courses, there are short quizzes that test your retention of the material. Learners will receive a certification of completion after each course once they are completed. These courses are only available in English at this time. **2.[Beginner's Guide to CLO on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLqL8Ymi3Z68Dqra76a_j0Y_WCcD5WSq4J): **With this free 4-part web tutorial, our expert designers will equip you with all the skills you need to get started using CLO. This training tutorial is made with CLO version 5.0. **3\. Youtube tutorial with sound guide available** * [**CLO features**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lfhIOk6s2Z4&list=PLqL8Ymi3Z68BJ-FaN2fdnUoSZ4qrFqzCk):[ ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lfhIOk6s2Z4&list=PLqL8Ymi3Z68BJ-FaN2fdnUoSZ4qrFqzCk)This playlist includes all the tools in the CLO 3D window, and how to use them * [**CLO tips and tricks**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zYV19dq6NR8&list=PLqL8Ymi3Z68CheCSgecHS1hR0YzAnJcIj): This playlist includes tutorial videos for intermediate to advanced CLO users looking to learn tips for creating and expressing various garments in CLO *You can also search for tutorial videos in various languages on [the CLO Youtube channel](https://www.youtube.com/c/CLO3D). **4\. Additional Online training resources** * **[Manual](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/categories/115000064648-Manual)** \-- Find step-by-step instructions for CLO features. * [Community](https://connect.clo-set.com/community) \-- Gain insights and share your expertise with CLO users. * **[Youtube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/user/clo3dsoftware)** \-- Find more video-based tutorials from beginning to advance. **5\. Webinar and Workshop** You can find bespoke training events by area and language [here.](https://linkin.bio/itsclo3d) **6.[CONNECT](https://connect.clo-set.com/) \- Digital sourcing platform for CLO users** If you'd rather prefer bespoke training, I advise you to reach out to users in[ CONNECT](https://connect.clo-set.com/) as I know some of them offer online training. *CLO offers customized training for **Enterprise clients.** Please reach out to your CLO Business representative for further information, scheduling, and pricing. Please check our [Learning page](https://clo3d.com/en/learning) for more information.
content_description: Discover a variety of training resources, including online courses, tutorials, and community support, to help you learn and master CLO 3D design.

title: Windows - CLO Network Version Installation
content: **Objective** Install Windows - CLO Network Version. Any Asset downloaded in the previous version is maintained when a new version is installed (ver5.0.0.) ** Operation** 1. Run the DVD received upon purchase or the install file received via email. 2. After running the install file, press "Next" on the setup window to continue installation. ![1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338848/1.png) 3. Review the License Agreement and click "I Agree" to accept the terms of the agreement. ![2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338868/2.png) 4. Choose a location to install the program. ![3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338908/3.png) 5. Select a Start Menu folder. ![4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298687/4.png) 6. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. ![5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338888/5.png) 7. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. ![6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298667/6.png) 8. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. 9. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: [ ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)[![accpage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001356347/accpage.png) ](http://localhost:1947/)If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: [Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95)As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. ![configuration.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336948/configuration.png) 10. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. ![accesstoremote.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336928/accesstoremote.png) 11. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. 12. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. ![sentinelkey.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001337068/sentinelkey.png) **※ Note:** ** Identifying Server PC's IP Address ** Start (Windows) Button ▶ All Programs ▶ Accessories ▶ Command Prompt ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>

title: Convert to Curve Point
content: **Easily convert Segment Points on the patterns to Curve Points, or Curve Points to Segment Points** **** 1. Right-click on the segment point with ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166904035609) **Edit Pattern** tool or on the curve point with ![Edit Curve Point On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40166914856217)**Edit Curve Point** tool. 2. title: How do you fit 3D Garments in CLO?
content: **Question** How do you fit 3D Garments in CLO? **Answer** To check fit, [create and drape](quick%20start%20link) 3D Garments first. [Draft](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000642008) your own Patterns in CLO or import Patterns created in other 2D CAD software to CLO, and then sew and drape Patterns on an Avatar. For more accurate fitting process, please use the Attach to [Avatar Tape](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000716827-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%ED%85%8C%EC%9D%B4%ED%94%84) function to align the 3D Garment's shoulder seams to the Avatar's shoulder line. Then, select the desired texture rendering style from Transparent Surface, Fit Map, Stress Map, and Strain Map, and use various types of Garment Measure to further examine the fit.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create, drape, and accurately fit 3D garments in CLO, including tips on pattern drafting, avatar alignment, and texture rendering options.

Adjust the [avatar size](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360013257553-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EC%A6%88-%EC%A1%B0%EC%A0%88-ver5-0-0-%EC%9D%B4%EC%83%81-) after draping the 3D garment on the avatar. 2. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Re-drape 3D Arrangement** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Auto_Draping.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36791452508313) **Re-drape 3D Arrangement** → Patterns are auto draped on the avatar based on its size.

title: Dart / Base Dart
content: ### Objective Create darts inside patterns. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Dart / Base Dart**** **2D Toolbar ▶![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360061084034) **Dart /![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360061084054) Base Dart (ver 5.2)** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. 2. Click and drag within a pattern to create a dart. 3. Or click once within the pattern. → The **Create Dart** window appears. 4. Enter the desired values for the following options. **Dimension** | Determine width (left), width (right), height (up), height (down). All values are measured from the center of the dart. ---|--- **Position** | **Outline** | Designate the dart's position within the pattern by entering the margin between the dart outline and the pattern outline (ver2.5.0). **Center** | Designate the dart's position within the pattern by entering the distance between the center of the dart and the pattern outline (ver2.5.0).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating darts within patterns using the 2D Pattern tool in CLO 3D.

title: 2D Seam Allowance

title: Modes
content: There are three available modes in the upper right dropdown menu of the CLO window: **Simulation** , **Print Layout** , and **Emulator**. **** In **Simulation** mode**,** it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D window, and in the 3D window drape garments, edit poses, or perform various other actions. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306927/_____.png)** In**Print Layout** mode, you can manually place patterns on prints to match texture placements, calculate fabric consumption, and create printable pattern layouts. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306987/_______.png)** In**Emulator** mode, you can enter the values of fabrics created with the CLO Fabric Kit (the precursor of the new CLO zFab Kit.) **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000303148/_____.png)**
content_description: Explore the three versatile modes of the CLO window—Simulation, Print Layout, and Emulator—to enhance your pattern creation, garment visualization, and fabric management experience.

title: [View Control] Zoom In/Out, Rotation
content: **Objective** In CLO, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. ** Operation** **Move![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788308/3D_Pan.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762547/17______.png) Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. **Zoom In/Out![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762587/3D_Zoom.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001762567/18______.png) Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). **※ Note:** Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) **Rotate![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788288/3D_Rotate.png)** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001788328/19___________.png) Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
content_description: Explore the versatile control methods for navigating and customizing your 3D experience in CLO, using mouse functions to move, zoom, and rotate the screen efficiently.

title: 2D Settings
content: Set settings related to 2D features. 1. Click Setting ▶ User Settings ▶ **2D** in the top menu. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Pattern** | **Default Particle Distance** | Set the default particle distance when creating patterns. **Automatically Offset 2D Patterns when Cut** | Toggle the option to offset 2D patterns when the Cut function is used, making it easier to work with UV export (ver3.2.0). **Notch** | **Display Type** | Configure how notches appear in the 2D window. **Length Fixed to Screen** | Notch length is fixed to the screen. The notch length does not change according to changes in the screen size (zoom-in or zoom-out.) When this option is toggled ON, [the Notch Length option disappears from the Property Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013369268). **Actual Length** | Notch length is fixed to its setting. The notch length changes when screen size is changed (zoom-in or zoom-out.) When this option is toggled OFF, [the Notch Length option appears in the Property Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013369268). **Default Notch Length** | Set the default notch length when creating notches. **📝Note:** Select Actual Length for Display Type to activate this setting. **Default Notch Type** | Set the default notch shape when creating notches. **Seam Allowance** | **Default Seam Allowance Width** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59567752850329) Set the default seam allowance width when creating seam allowances. **📝Note:** The seam allowance width can be set from 6 to 250 mm.
content_description: Configure and customize 2D feature settings to enhance your design experience and streamline pattern creation.

title: Convert to Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Convert to Avatar Load 3D Body File Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar Save Converted Avatar **Convert to Avatar ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EVmOocECOL8 \- Convert 3D dummies or body scans to CLO avatars maintaining their body shapes. \- Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar ** **Load 3D Body file ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Biv28X6TBA4 \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar** \- Load a 3D body file, preferably in attention pose, as a reference for the conversion. \- Select the CLO Avatar to be converted with the 3D body file. \- Click **Next**. **Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar ** * **Change Avatar Pose ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b8fAbFMeGzo - Select the Pose folder corresponding to the loaded Avatar. \- Load attention pose. \- Check **Joint Rotation Only** and select **OK**. * **Align Height and Inseam with Avatar Size Editor ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adQH_A6I5vg \- Select **Open Avatar Size Editor**. \- Adjust **Height** to align the shoulder height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Adjust **Inseam** to align the crotch height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Once the adjustment is completed, close the Avatar Size Editor. * **Align Avatar Joints** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yrn7-Ttwy9Q \- Align all joints: total body, ankle, arm, and neck. \- Make sure to align above four locations as closely as possible for more accurate conversion. \- Select **Convert** once all adjustments are completed. **Save Converted Avatar ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxF61xDL60k \- Rotate to check the quality of the converted avatar. \- Click **Save as Avatar** to save the converted avatar when it's satisfactory. \- When additional modification is needed, click **Back** to repeat previous steps. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for converting 3D body files into CLO avatars, detailing each step from loading files to saving the final converted avatar.

title: Does CLO have an online community?
content: **Yes, CLO has an active and supportive community!** The CLO community is made up of users from all over the world! From beginners to experienced professionals, who share knowledge, ask questions, and exchange tips about using CLO. ### **Where Can You Find the CLO Community?** * [**CONNECT** ](https://connect.clo-set.com/community)is CLO’s official community platform, where users can: * Interact, ask questions, and share their projects. * Offer or request personalized training. * Participate in **challenges.** * Explore inspiring **user stories.** * Browse or post on the **job board.** * Stay updated with events, news, and more. * **[CLO Discord](https://discord.com/invite/CujT8B5m5g)** offers real-time interaction between community members and CLO designers. It’s a place to: * Chat casually or get quick help. * Discuss tips and workflows. * Share feedback and feature requests. * Get support from experienced users and CLO staff. ### **Why Join the Community?** Being part of the CLO community helps you: * Learn faster from experienced users; * Connect with professionals in the digital fashion industry. * * * If you have any questions, please [Contact Us.](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus)
content_description: Discover and engage with a vibrant global community of CLO users, where you can share knowledge, seek support, and enhance your skills in digital fashion design.

title: Texture Generator (ver 7.1)
content: **List of Contents** **Open Texture ** **Select Area of Texture** **Set Options** **Save Texture Image** **Apply Texture** **Objective** Seamlessly generate texture maps with scanned or captured images, and check the results in real-time within the 3D window. **Location**** ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13169546878617) Texture Generator **Operation ** **Open Texture** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → Texture Generator Opens. 2. Click Open at the left bottom of Texture Generator to open the texture image. → The size and resolution of the textures loaded are displayed at the top. → For XTEX files, other maps (Normal map, Opacity map etc.) in the folder are automatically loaded. **Select Area of Texture** 1. Find and click on the minimum area where the fabric pattern repeats. ▶ Drag to select. → The optimized result analyzed within the selected area will show up. → The analyzed result is repeated in the preview window at the bottom. 2. To adjust the area, move the point of the selected area. → It is analyzed automatically again within the selected area. 3. To maintain the selected area, click Manual at the right bottom of the selected area. → The selected area is maintained and repeated. **Set Options** The options below can be set only in Auto mode since they work based on the analyzed results. * **Fabric Type ** Select fabric type for more accurate analysis. The analysis is based on Normal Map, thus it is only vaild with the existence of Normal Map. \- Plain: Solid fabric without repeated patterns. \- Repeat Pattern: Fabric pattern is regular. \- Random Color Pattern: Fabric pattern is irregular. * **Equalize ** Adjust the value to equalize the difference in brightness caused by crease in the fabric. ※ Note: Depending on the fabric, some colors or patterns may be distorted. Refer to the attached image. below. ![seamless_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171432946713) * **Smooth ** When the connected part of the fabrics are not smooth by crease in the fabric, align weave areas equally. ![image-20221201-064052.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13171781957657) * **Show/Hide Grid ** Click Show/Hide icon in Preview window at the bottom to check the grid of the repeated texture. **Save Texture Image** 1. Click Save at the bottom to save the generated texture as Image file. → Save Textures window appears. 2. Select the textures and map type to save and click OK button. → Each map name is automatically applied after the set name and saved as PNG files. **Apply Texture** 1. When the texture generating is complete, click the Apply & Close button at the bottom right of Texture Generator. → The texture is applied to the fabric simultaneously and the Texture generator is closed.
content_description: Create and manipulate seamless texture maps from scanned images for real-time visualization in a 3D environment.

title: Dart
content: **List of Contents** Dart Create Dart Create Dart with Specific Values **Dart** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wu-cknKD5zw \- Create Dart on Patterns. Because Patterns can be sewn without seam allowances in CLO, Dart will be sewn with the Pattern outlines. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021854067/mceclip0.png) **Dart** tool from the 2D toolbar or navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Dart.** ** Create Dart** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTPxmGmM-7E \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021854067/mceclip0.png) **Dart** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and click and drag within a Pattern. \- The preview of the Dart will appear. \- Release the mouse to complete the Dart. **Create Dart with Specific Values** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Zw15iDys3Q \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021854067/mceclip0.png) **Dart** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and click once within a Pattern. \- The Create Dart window will appear. \- Enter desired values to the Create Dart window and select OK. * **Size** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=silafU2IVJo \- Assign Width (Left), Width (Right), Height (Up), and Height (Down) which are measured from the center of the Dart. * **Position** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-l1vyDxjqks \- Assign the placement of the Dart. * **Outline** \- Enter Left, Right, Up, and Down values which indicate the margin between the Dart and the Pattern outline. * **Center** \- Enter Left, Right, Up, and Down values which are measured from the center of the Dart Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to creating and customizing darts in CLO 3D, featuring step-by-step instructions and instructional YouTube videos.
